sections.title: Design-Bid-Build Procurement
sections.body: Construction documents for shallow foundations in the design-bid-build procurement method include plans, specifications, and estimates.
key_points: Design-bid-build is the traditional procurement method for shallow foundation construction
Construction documents include plans, specifications, and estimates
sections.applicability: General guidance on construction document preparation for shallow foundation projects.

sections.title: Plans, Specifications and Estimates
sections.body: Plans are typically developed to show footing locations, dimensions, steel reinforcement details, required footing elevations, and embedment and backfill dimensions. A foundation data sheet should show summary subsurface data in spatial relation to the foundations. Material descriptions, groundwater levels, SPT data and other subsurface investigation information are particularly valuable to the contractor for evaluation of excavation, shoring, dewatering, and other construction details. The geotechnical report should be made available to contractors. Plans should detail drainage and backfill requirements for abutments and retaining walls, including prevention of the 'bump at the end of the bridge' by specifying properly compacted, non-erodible abutment backfill. Specifications typically include requirements for concrete, steel reinforcement and construction procedures. FHWA Standard Specifications (FHWA, 1996) cover Section 208 (Structure Excavation and Backfill for Major Structures), Section 209 (Structure Excavation and Backfill), Section 552 (Structural Concrete), and Section 554 (Reinforcing Steel). Specifications should reference the geotechnical report and include special provisions for foundation soil/rock treatment or groundwater control where needed. Pay items may include Structure Excavation, Foundation Fill, Structural Backfill, Shoring and Bracing, and Cofferdams.
key_points: Plans show footing locations, dimensions, reinforcement, elevations, and backfill details
Foundation data sheet should show subsurface data in spatial relation to foundations
Geotechnical report should be made available to contractors
Abutment backfill must be properly compacted and not prone to fine-grained material migration
Underdrain filter or geocomposite drains prevent fine-grained soil migration behind stemwalls
FHWA Standard Specifications: Section 208, 209 (excavation/backfill), 552 (concrete), 554 (reinforcing steel)
Special provisions needed for foundation soil/rock treatment or groundwater control
Common pay items: Structure Excavation, Foundation Fill, Structural Backfill, Shoring/Bracing, Cofferdams
sections.applicability: Preparing plans, specifications and pay items for shallow foundation construction contracts.

sections.title: Structural Fills
sections.body: Special details and specifications are necessary when constructing a compacted structural fill to support a bridge foundation such as an abutment. Figure 9-1 (adapted from Cheney and Chassie, 2000) shows recommended details for construction of a structural approach embankment, including zones of specified materials and compaction requirements. The materials specifications are chosen to provide a firm, non-yielding condition suitable for bridge abutment spread footing support. The specification for select material is from the Soils and Foundations Workshop Reference Manual (Cheney & Chassie, 2000) and is included in Appendix A. Specifications from Washington, Nevada, and Michigan DOTs for structural fills beneath spread footing abutments are also in Appendix A. Select structural fill and highway embankment material should not include unsuitable material such as peat, muck, wood, organic waste, coal, charcoal, or any other deleterious material.
key_points: Structural fill specifications are critical for bridge abutment spread footing support
Figure 9-1 shows recommended structural approach embankment details
Three zones: Select Structural Fill (100% compaction T99), Highway Embankment 150mm topsize (95% T180), Highway Embankment (90% T180)
1.5 m pad of select material placed beneath abutments on spread footings
Minimum 15 m of embankment placed before abutment construction or pile driving
Embankment and select material placed simultaneously at vertical payment line
Unsuitable materials (peat, muck, wood, organic waste, coal, charcoal) must be excluded
State DOT specifications (WA, NV, MI) for structural fills are in Appendix A

figures.title: Structural Approach Fill Details
figures.description: Cross-section showing recommended structural approach embankment construction details (after Cheney & Chassie, 2000). Shows Select Structural Fill (100% T99), Highway Embankment Material 150mm topsize (95% T180), and Highway Embankment Material (90% T180) zones. Minimum breakpoint of berm 0.6 m above footing top and 1.2 m from front edge. 1.5 m select material pad beneath abutments. 15 m minimum embankment prior to abutment construction. 3H:1V minimum end slope.

sections.applicability: Specifying structural fill materials and compaction requirements for bridge abutments on spread footings.

sections.title: Design-Build Procurement
sections.body: The design-build procurement approach should include owner-provided geotechnical data sufficient for foundation design. A Geotechnical Data Report (GDR) is recommended, and Geotechnical Interpretive Reports and Geotechnical Baseline Reports may also be prepared to document expected surface and subsurface conditions, reduce uncertainty during bidding, and reduce risk contingencies. The GDR should identify special conditions affecting structural fill and shallow foundation design/construction and provide test results for necessary geotechnical properties. Because alignment and structure locations may not be fixed in design-build procurement, the contractor may need to provide supplemental explorations and testing. Special Provision specifications should include requirements for codified design criteria, tolerable settlement criteria, estimated scour depths, seismic criteria, adherence to standard specifications, and a submittal and review process with minimum quality control and assurance plan.
key_points: Design-build procurement requires owner-provided geotechnical data (GDR recommended)
Geotechnical Interpretive Reports and Baseline Reports reduce bidding uncertainty and risk
GDR should identify special conditions and provide necessary geotechnical test results
Contractor may need supplemental explorations if alignment/structure locations are not fixed
Special Provisions should include: design criteria, settlement criteria, scour depths, seismic criteria
Submittal and review process with QC/QA plan should be prescribed
Specifications should impose contractor requirements to achieve desired foundation performance
sections.applicability: Preparing geotechnical documents and specifications for design-build shallow foundation projects.
